capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction and use the canonical representations already built into Mathlib.

- For the factorization statement, separate \(n=0\). Otherwise, if the \(p\)-coordinate of `Nat.factorization n` were nonzero, then \(p\) would divide \(n\). Since \(n>0\), divisibility gives \(p \le n\), contradicting \(n<p\). A suitable `Nat.factorization` support/vanishing lemma should package this argument.

- For the local-ring statement, use that the order-top point of `PrimeSpectrum R` is constructed from the unique maximal ideal of a local ring. Reduce the equality through `PrimeSpectrum.asIdeal`; after unfolding or applying the relevant `top`/`asIdeal` lemma, both sides are the same ideal. If definitional simplification is insufficient, prove ideal equality by extensionality and use the uniqueness characterization of `IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal`.

The only small edge case is \(n=0\), because the usual “nonzero factorization coordinate implies divisibility” lemma may require \(n\ne0\).
